title: Rewire Cables to Join the Network
statement:
An office has n machines numbered 0 to n − 1. Each cables[i] = [a, b] is a cable joining machines a and b. Two machines can talk if a chain of cables links them.

In one move you unplug any existing cable and plug it in between any two machines. Return the fewest moves needed so that every machine can talk to every other one. If there are not enough cables to ever do it, return -1.

examples.why: The triangle 0–1–2 has one cable it does not need. Move it to join 2 and 3.
Linking 4 machines takes at least 3 cables, and there are only 2.
Machines 4 and 5 are alone, so three groups need 2 joins. The group 0, 1, 2, 3 holds 5 cables where 3 would do, so its 2 spare cables are exactly enough.

hints: When is it impossible, no matter how cleverly you move cables?
If there are at least n − 1 cables, there is always a spare one to move. Each move can join two separate groups.
Answer: −1 if cables < n − 1, otherwise (number of connected groups) − 1. Count groups with union-find or DFS.

explain.intuition:
Connecting n machines needs at least n − 1 cables, so with fewer the answer is −1, whatever the layout. With at least n − 1 cables there is always enough spare cabling: if you have c groups, the groups use at least n − c cables to hold themselves together, which leaves at least c − 1 spare ones inside cycles.

Each move can join two groups, and it can never join more than two. So the answer is exactly groups − 1. Where the cables currently are does not matter beyond how many groups they form.
steps: Create a union-find over the n machines with groups = n.
For each cable, union its ends; when two different roots merge, decrease groups.
pitfalls: Counting the spare cables and returning that. The answer depends on the number of groups, not on the number of spare cables (example 1 has one spare, example 3 has two spares and needs two).
Forgetting isolated machines with no cables at all. They are groups too.
Running recursive DFS on 100 000 machines in a chain. Use union-find or an explicit stack.

solutions.title: Count groups with DFS
solutions.idea: Build adjacency lists and count connected components with an explicit stack.

solutions.title: Union-find
solutions.idea: Start with n groups; every cable that joins two different groups reduces the count by one.

followups: Return the actual moves: which cable to unplug and where to plug it.
Cables now have a cost per length and moving one costs that much. How does the problem change?
lcTitle: Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
